r8-gate-ordering.title: Hard/soft gate ordering in run
r8-gate-ordering.imperative: Read the code to confirm a predict/optimize failure structurally cannot reach explain in cmd_run -- no broad try/except swallowing the chain. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r8-gate-ordering.finding: Read cmd_run (race_week.py:227-249) directly: 4 sequential statements, sessions_checkpoint=_do_collect_check(...); prediction_checkpoint=_do_predict(...); lineup_report=_do_optimize(...); explain_result=_do_explain(...) -- no try/except anywhere in cmd_run. If _do_predict or _do_optimize raises, Python's normal control flow means the exception propagates immediately and the following line(s), including _do_explain, never execute -- this is a language guarantee, not a convention that could be silently violated. main()'s only try/except (line 360) wraps args.func(args) at the CLI boundary and just prints+returns 1 on any exception; it does not call explain in its except branch. No broad try/except around the whole chain exists anywhere in the file.

r9-resumption.title: Resumption: --force vs hash-mismatch distinct paths
r9-resumption.imperative: Confirm --force and a real hash mismatch are two distinct code paths to a rerun, not conflated. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r9-resumption.finding: _do_predict/_do_optimize both use: 'if not args.force and stages.should_skip_stage(existing, upstream): skip'. Truth-table traced: force=True -> 'not force' is False -> short-circuits, ALWAYS reruns regardless of hash state (force path independent of hash). force=False, hash matches -> should_skip_stage True -> skips. force=False, hash mismatches -> should_skip_stage False -> reruns WITHOUT force (hash-mismatch path independent of force). These are genuinely two distinct triggers to the same 'rerun' outcome, not conflated -- confirmed by the 4 separate tests (force-reruns-even-when-fresh, hash-mismatch-reruns-without-force, for both predict and optimize) which I re-ran and observed pass in r3/r11.
